key_insight: Ultra-precise structural analysis reveals subsurface buckling at 0.25 ML oxygen coverage and explains how nano-domain scattering conceals the true periodicity of the 0.50 ML phase on Rh(100).
engineering_relevance: Resolving oxygen adsorption and ordering on catalytically important Rh(100) provides more reliable atomic structures for surface-reaction modeling.
method: Quantitative low-energy electron diffraction (LEED) structure analysis.
Variable-temperature scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) and density functional theory (DFT).
Short-range-order simulations of coherent nano-domain scattering.
evidence_signal: LEED achieved single-digit-picometer structural precision with Pendry R factors near 0.07, while simulations showed how nano-domains virtually extinguish diffraction spots.
watch_item: The 0.50 ML phase forms many nano-domains already below 100 K, making diffraction-based identification of its true periodicity temperature- and ordering-sensitive.
paper_title: Oxygen on Rh(100) revisited with ultra-high precision
